phx.summary: Impressive as it was to see Suns recover from the Houston loss by winning at Denver, Nash's quote after that Rockets defeat is worrisome: 'I'm not helping us very much on one leg.'
Nash says his hamstring is feeling a little better. Better yet, after a nice win at Memphis, Suns are quietly 8-3 since the All-Star break, beating Spurs, Pistons, Sonics, Mavs and Nuggets.
Suns play 10 of their final 13 games at home. Of course, as good as they are on the road -- leading the league at 29-8 -- maybe that closing sked helps San Antonio more than Phoenix.
The run-and-gunners have scored 120-plus points 18 times. Suns did it only 10 times in the previous seven seasons.
With a series looming against a team (Memphis) they don't like to play, Suns can be thankful for one thing. After two straight L's to GS, at least Suns don't have to see Warriors in Round 1.
So they didn't maintain that 31-4 pace. Big deal. Suns following up that sick start with a 30-15 burst looks quite sufficient.

mia.summary: How hot are Heat? Try this hot: Miami hasn't lost a game in regulation since Feb. 1. Heat's only two losses in the past 17 games came in overtime -- and both without Shaq.
First team to win 50 games this season. First team to clinch a playoff berth this season. First team to post two 10-game win streaks this season. In short, no one's hotter.
Sorry. Don't care how impressive Heat looked winning at Suns' pace. Lose to Charlotte the next night and you forfeit No. 1.
In case you still need convincing that Shaq makes a difference, be advised that Heat had only 13 road wins last season ... compared to 22 already with five road games left.
Heat would never be this low if Shaq were playing. More than one cynic, mind you, has wondered aloud about whether Shaq is really ill or simply saving some fuel for the playoffs.
S. Van Gundy is undoubtedly panicky about the way his Heat are stumbling to the finish line, but at least one recent trend is encouraging: Zo has averaged 23.2 mpg since April 8.

sas.summary: Common sense says they'll be back at No. 1 before long and enter the playoffs as the title favorite. But for now, until Duncan and Ginobili are healthy, Spurs can't go higher than this.
For the seventh straight full season, Spurs have won 50 games. But this group is only 1-3 without Duncan, so expect a longer rest after this ankle twist to ensure TD's playoff health.
Pop thinks Duncan will make an appearance during the final five games of the regular season. Dare we say, even without TD until the playoffs, Spurs will hang on to a top-two seed.
Spurs are nearly back to .500 without Duncan (5-6), and dare we also say Duncan can find a playoff rhythm quickly even if he doesn't play before the regular season ends.
Winning those back-to-back games in double OT -- the second without Manu and Duncan -- halted a 1-6 road skid and eased fears that Spurs could wind up blowing the Southwest lead.
It didn't always seem so with Duncan missing 16 games (9-7), but this actually was a fairly easy season for the most versatile Spurs yet. Forty of S.A.'s 59 wins are by 10 points or more.

okc.summary: Winning at MSG salvaged something from what had to be Sonics' worst week of the season. Holding a 10 1/2-game division lead over Denver doesn't hurt, either.
Trust us: Coach McMillan is far more concerned about the injury loss of Radmanovic than reports of the season's first locker-room grumbling about minutes, roles, shots, etc.
As hot as Nuggets are, look at Sonics' division lead. It's still nearly 10 games, in spite of stubborn Seattle's recent turmoil.
Wondering what keeps Sonics up here? Slump or not, injuries or not, Sonics are still 23-14 against .500-plus teams, second only to San Antonio's 26-14. Phoenix is third at 24-15.
This is no joke. Sonics haven't won since April 1 and have nothing but injuries (Rashard, Radmanovic, Daniels, Fortson).
It wasn't the smoothest divisional clinch, but c'mon. Fifty-two wins! Nate must have done some coaching to coax 52 wins out of a smallish squad universally picked to be a doormat.

det.summary: Pistons can't catch Miami, and chances are no one can catch Pistons and bump them out of the No. 2 spot. So it's as good a time as there is for Larry to take time off to get healthy.
Prince looks more like a Most Improved Player favorite every day ... and Gar Heard's fortunes as interim coach (3-0 in this fill-in stint compared to 2-4 last time) are improving, too.
Why is a Lakers comparison so apt for these switch-flippers? One Detroit observer we trust says the champs' problem is arrogance against lesser teams. Just like the old Lakers.
Pistons players can get frustrated with Larry, but they do miss him at times, too. To wit, they're 9-8 without him and followed up a 9-1 record February with a 9-8 March.
Instead of saying this is the win streak that proves Detroit Is Back, let's assume the champs have been so up-and-down because they've known for a while that Miami was uncatchable.
What's the highest compliment we can give the champs? They placed no one on the committee's All-NBA team, but even without a top-15 player they remain our pick to win the East.

hou.summary: Rockets are your proverbial Team O' The Week. Only problem with Houston's surge is that the No. 6 seed might prove more attractive than No. 5, depending on San Antonio's finish.
Rockets haven't been this far over .500 since 1996-97. But they really don't feel like celebrating after losing Juwan for a while.
All Rockets needed to finally seize No. 5 out West was a win over Duncan-less Spurs. Instead Houston joined Atlanta and Charlotte as the only teams to lose to SA with Duncan out.
Just when we were ready to anoint Houston as the Lower Seed No One Wants To Face out West, Rockets played New Orleans at home on April Fool's Day ... and lost. No joke.
The bad news? Rockets are 7-6 since losing Juwan for good. The good news? A win in Monday's road finale at Seattle would make this Houston's second-best road team ever at 25-16.
Postseason success, of course, is what really matters for T-Mac, who has never won a playoff series. But 50 wins would be nice, too. T-Mac's previous teams have never topped 45-37.

dal.summary: Banged-up Mavs have no time to get what their coach says they desperately need. Nellie's view: 'We need 20 games together. . . . We don't even know how to play with each other.'
Now that the baton has been passed, let's be real. Until Dampier and Stackhouse return, it probably doesn't matter who's coaching. Mavs won't be a factor without those two healthy.
Winner of the Dallas-Sacto season series has lost the teams' last three playoff matchups. So maybe Mavs (3-1 this season) would prefer seeing Houston in Round 1.
You can deal with a lopsided L at Cavs after Ws at Detroit, Boston and Philly -- in the same week Stack and Damp return.
Mavs are becoming a trendy pick to make playoff noise, but more impressive is how steady they've become. This is a fifth straight 50-win season, after just two in the club's first 20 years.
Don't say they have nothing to play for. Those increasingly confident Mavs are trying to finish ahead of Miami ... just in case they need home-court advantage in the Finals.

bos.summary: The defense can still be disappointing, but the numbers don't lie: Celts are 7-1 (and surging) since 'Toine's return.
Ricky Ricky is making a serious Sixth Man push. And Celts can't stop winning, even though they guard almost no one.
This might be an omen. The same week word leaks out that Celts want to add some black to their unis next season, they drop three straight and anger their coach with their cockiness.
If you got excited about the 11-1 start to the latest 'Toine Era (and we did) you have to be concerned by the 1-5 stumble since. And we are, especially now that 'Toine is hurt as well.
Peter May of the Boston Globe makes his usual strong case about Ricky Ricky playing too many minutes to be a true sixth man, but we still feel Davis hasn't received sufficient props.
The reward for Boston's first division crown since '91-92 looks like a first-round series with Indy for the third successive spring. Don't know that we'd call it a welcome reward, though.

mem.summary: How time flies: Gasol hasn't played since Jan. 22. Not sure how long this can last, but credit Grizz -- a gutty 12-8 without him.
Gasol and Bonzi are back, but it's clear that Grizz have an underrated bench and a coach who deserves COY consideration whether or not he has been there all season.
The club record for road wins in a season is 19. But after crashing at home to Hornets, it'll be tough for Grizz to win three more roadies, given their rough remaining schedule.
Swift is out suddenly and might be gone permanently when he hits free agency this summer. Will he be missed? Memphis is 10-8 when he's sidelined and 31-23 when he plays.
Gritty Grizz would have to run the table to match last season's 50 wins. But even if they don't this is the franchise's second-best season by a wide margin over No. 3 (28-54 in '02-03).
An 0-4 trip means Memphis backed into the playoffs a bit, but don't forget these guys do have road wins over Suns, Pistons and Spurs. Phoenix knows Grizz pose a physical threat.

den.summary: Nuggets are winning so much lately, George has little cause to be furious. Sunday's loss to Phoenix -- the second half of a back-to-back -- was the new coach's first home defeat.
Interesting stat: Nuggets now have more wins with Furious George in charge (18) than they had in the first 42 games (17).
The committee didn't believe it when some of our Nuggets pals said they were gunning for the seventh seed out West. But take a look: Denver is much closer to No. 7 than No. 9.
Throw out their last two games against Phoenix and Furious George has Nuggets on a stunning 17-0 run. Overall they're 14-1 at home for the new coach and 10-5 on the road.
Dare we say it's safe to anoint Denver as the proverbial Lower Seed No One Wants To Play. Nuggets are now  a ridiculous 21-0 since Feb. 23 . . . if you exclude two losses to Phoenix.
We don't want to worry Furious George, but the last team to post the best record after the All-Star break and lose in Round 1 was ... George's 1994 Sonics. To Denver, remember.

sac.summary: Just when Sacto thought its luck was turning -- with the disputed Bibby buzzer-beater to topple Memphis -- Miller goes down for perhaps the rest of the regular season. A killer blow.
At 7-7 since the Webber deal, and with Miller out now, you have to start wondering if Kings will slip all the way down to No. 7 and into a first-round series against (ugh) Spurs or Suns.
Our money's on Philly for the big Monday night showdown. Can't see Webber losing both games to his old team.
Kings apparently need more games against Philly. They've looked tough both times they saw Webber, but the fact remains that Sac is 13-16 since checking in at 32-14 on Feb. 4.
Peja has picked it up (24.6 ppg in his last nine), and Kings, after looking as though they could drop all the way to No. 7 out West, have averaged 119 points in their last five games.
Wouldn't be Kings playoff season without injuries: B. Miller, B. Jackson and now Peja. Chances are they all play in the playoffs; chances are better none of them will be 100 percent.

was.summary: Only six teams in the East have winning records against the West. And Wiz (12-11) are one of them, behind only Miami (15-10), Detroit (15-10) and Orlando (14-10).
With six of seven on the road and Jamison ailing, Wiz face the threat of joining Cleveland, Chicago and Orlando on the slide.
Looks like they got the right Jordan this time. Eddie likely won't win Coach of the Year, but he has Wiz off to a 2-2 start on a crucial five-game trip ... without the injured Jamison.
If healthy, Wiz have the playoff capacity to entertain if nothing else. Arenas-Jamison-Hughes ranks as the NBA's highest scoring trio by five points over Amare-Marion-Johnson.
After four 43-point games, Arenas finally reached 44. Problem is, Wiz are 1-4 in those five games, so they need to get back to balance if they want to do something in the playoffs.
References to '97-98 don't apply to Bulls only. Until now, Wiz haven't had a winning season since His Airness retired, either.

chi.summary: Air Gordon is what they're apparently calling Chicago's surprising rookie sixth man. Let's see if they're still winning enough by the end of a crazy March to be passing out nicknames.
After going 7-4 in February, Bulls are 4-7 in March and still have seven more games to play this month. And it hasn't helped matters that they're 0-4 against New Jersey.
Winning five in a row at this point -- three on the road -- is as impressive as anything these Bulls have achieved. So it's almost time, for the first time since '98, to print up playoff tickets.
It looks safer and safer to put the 0-9 No Mores in the same club with Phoenix when it comes to making the playoffs after a dreadful start. Suns, remember, opened 0-13 in '96-97.
We can understand Jerry Reinsdorf's concerns about spending big on Curry and Chandler. But someone is going to have to explain why Skiles doesn't have a long-term extension yet.
Don't write Baby Bulls off in the first round, even without Curry and Deng. They're 14-2 since a worrisome four-game skid.

cle.summary: After halting that six-game skid by pounding Orlando and Indiana, Cavs (their fans, actually) face the prospect of another letdown Tuesday if Boozer isn't in the building.
This probably isn't the week that pressure will ease on anyone in Cleveland. Cavs could be flirting with .500 after a home date with Detroit and trips to Houston and Dallas.
Cavs haven't won a road game, for any coach, since Jan. 22. And none of the 10 teams they've beaten on the road -- not one -- has had a winning record when the game was played.
One overlooked factor that led to the coaching change: Silas came to Cleveland promising second-half surges from his teams ... but Cavs faded in both of his seasons.
Of all their many issues, nothing is stranger than McInnis falling in and out (and back in) favor. When Cavs just missed last season's playoffs, McInnis' injury was seen as the killer blow.
Gone might be Cavs' first winning record since '97-98. LeBron's Cavs now face becoming just the second team in history to drop out of the playoffs from 10 games over .500 after 50 games.

lal.summary: Lakers' playoff chances would have been boosted by a trade at the deadline, but Kobe has scored at least 32 points in five straight. L.A. is 4-1 in those games and, thus, hanging in there.
Orlando was 45-37 in its first season without Shaq. Lakers, presently on a 40-42 pace, would probably make the playoffs if they could somehow match that Magic effort.
Lakers went 6-8 in the 14 games Kobe missed. So you can't suggest that was the stretch that doomed L.A.'s playoff bid, because its 14 games this month have been uglier (4-10).
Odom's out. Kobe's freshly injured. The schedule won't let up. So it's all but official: Lakers won't be able to avoid just their fourth non-playoff season since moving to L.A. in 1960.
Another fave (L.A. Times' Mark Heisler) points out that Boston ''all but invented this league'' yet hasn't won a title since '86. Meaning you have to be lucky and good to return to glory.
Lakers are actually a robust 27-6 when they hold the opposition under 100 points. Unfortunately there's the small matter of how poorly they defended in those other 47 games.

orl.summary: Heartwarming as it would be to see Grant Hill back on the playoff stage, Orlando's ongoing struggles are actually the biggest source of postseason hope in Philly and Indy these days.
Francis. Augmon. Weisbrod v. T-Mac. A coaching change. Things are unraveling so fast for this former feel-good team and poor Grant Hill that you don't know where to start.
It's one thing if you fire a coach in March and you have Brendan Malone to take over. It's another when Johnny Davis, like him or not, is replaced by someone with no experience.
Maybe the unraveling is subsiding, although we suspect that Saturday's victory in Jersey did more to hurt Nets' playoff bid than help a Magic team missing Hill, Hedo and Jameer.
These guys are tough to console with Hill and Hedo out and the playoffs all but gone, but no one can take away Orlando's more-than-respectable record of 15-15 against the West.
Like Frank Hamblen says to all moms: ''Don't let your sons grow up to be interim coaches.'' Injury-ravaged Magic are 4-12 under Jent after losing six straight before he took over.

phi.summary: Webber's taking the heat, but it's Iverson's MVP campaign that'll take the big hit if Sixers miss out on the playoffs.
Our man Stephen A. has put the heat squarely on Coach O'Brien. But perhaps this thumb injury is just the sort of bizarro-world spark Iverson needs to carry Philly into the playoffs.
Why all the gloom and doom? Philly's on a 6-2 surge, with a 3�-game lead on the only team that can really catch up (Nets).
The pressure's on AI, and not just because of Webb's shoulder. This could be the first time since '76-77 that the league's top two scorers (AI and Kobe) miss the playoffs.
Iverson has essentially clinched the scoring title, but this is still a big week for Sixers with games against the team they're chasing (home to Celtics) and the team chasing them (at Nets).
As promised Friday, Iverson will get LeBron's spot on our MVP ballot and our All-NBA first team if Sixers make it and Cavs miss out. Which looks like a lock now, doesn't it?

ind.summary: For the first time since 1972, the state has no team in the NCAA Tournament. And if Jermaine's shoulder doesn't heal soon, Pacers won't be cheering up anyone in the nation's heartland.
Carlisle won't win 50 games for the first time in four seasons, but he has to be a Coach of the Year factor if Pacers can make the playoffs after all they've been through.
How good a coaching job has Carlisle done? Consider that Pacers' projected starting lineup of Tinsley, Miller, Artest, Foster and O'Neal has combined to play zero games together.
The way these guys are rolling without J. O'Neal -- specifically Reggie, who averaged 19.1 ppg in 31.2 mpg in March -- Pacers have to be the East's most feared bracket buster.

This will be the first team in history (full seasons only) with fewer than 52 wins after a 60-win season, but we repeat: Carlisle has never coached better, keeping Indy over .500 on its roller coaster.
Losing to Miami in Jermaine's return, after Shaq got hurt, was a bit of a downer. Here's the pick-me-up: Pacers went on a season-saving run of 15-7 while their O'Neal was out injured.

min.summary: This might just be us jumping the gun, but it sure looks (to us) like Wolves just want the season to be over with.
Under Flip, Wolves were a game under .500. Under McHale, they're 9-8 and (uh-oh) four behind Denver in the loss column.
The good news? Wolves apparently haven't quit. The bad news? They probably waited too long to find a groove.
Did you see KG on TV after the win at Sac? His enthusiastic warning about Wolves ''coming'' strikes us as a good sign; it was the most KG-esque bravado we've seen from him for ages.
It's probably time for the committee (of one) to stop going on TV and saying Minny still has a shot at the No. 8 spot. KG's Wolves, in reality, aren't any more alive than Kobe's Lakers.
Here's a hunch that the best record of any non-playoff team isn't much consolation. Another hunch: McHale resigns as coach and GM, leaving Wolves to fill both posts before anything else.

lac.summary: If they can manage a 13-6 finish -- a tad optimistic, true -- Clips can halt a league-worst run of 11 straight losing seasons.
Clippers really could have been a contender for No. 8, but they can't win the close ones for the umpteenth straight season. Twelve of L.A.'s last 16 losses are by five points or less.
A letter writer to the LA Times says Kobe didn't choose Lakers over Clips; he turned Lakers into Clips. The standings back  up the claim: Clips are only a half-game behind their neighbors.
Only four times in franchise history -- twice in Buffalo and twice in L.A. -- have Braves/Clips finished with a better record than Lakers. The last time it happened: 1992-93.
A league-leading 12th straight losing season is unavoidable now. But finishing No. 1 in the Staples Center standings will almost certainly work as consolation for these guys.
The magic number to clinch a better record than their Staples Center co-tenants is one. And if not for a season-long injury epidemic, it probably wouldn't have been close.

bkn.summary: It hasn't been a pretty month in Jersey. You don't hear much talk about the playoffs now after four heavy losses (by an average of 20.3 ppg) and a near-loss at New Orleans.
Just when it appeared you could exclude Jersey from playoff consideration, this is the only Eastern Conference resident outside the top three on any kind of roll.
Whether or not Nets claim that No. 8 spot, they have to be somewhat encouraged by their 19-17 record since losing Jefferson. Jersey easily could have folded instead.
The more we think about it, the harder it is to see how snaring the East's final playoff berth will make a huge difference to Kidd when it comes to his wanting to stay or go.
Nets haven't visited the .500 Club since Nov. 9. But they're closing in on it now and can secure a franchise-record-tying fourth straight winning season with a 4-1 finish.
The way Nets are rolling, it looks as though they'll snare the eighth spot. But if they don't, Nets can point to a league-leading 13 losses in which they led by at least 10 points.

nyk.summary: You hate to be negative after Knicks' longest home winning streak (seven) since the spring of 2001. But the fact remains that they're 0-13 against teams at the .600 level or better.
Bold prediction II: Three losing seasons is about to become four, because Knicks -- with just two road wins in 2005 -- have way too many roadies left (10) to finish 14-4.
We like Herb as much as anyone, but c'mon. Everyone saying he deserves the job full-time forgets that Knicks still lose a lot of close games and haven't exactly made a playoff charge.
More bad news for Steph. Suns' success makes it three straight teams to win at least 50 games in their first full season after Steph leaves (along with Wolves and Nets).
Did J-Kidd really add any lasting spice to the rivalry by calling Knicks ''a bad team''? Who can argue with him? Nets have won 17 of the past 20 meetings; NY has four straight losing seasons.
On Jan. 1, at 16-13, a playoff berth seemed reasonable. Zeke's Knicks have won only 16 games since, and only that many because they're 3-0 on the road after a 2-20 away stretch.

mil.summary: The month basically breaks down this way so far: Redd hasn't missed much; Bucks haven't defended much.
Life on the road is as big an issue as any. Milwaukee is just 7-25 in away games, with all seven wins coming against East foes.
After an 0-5 trip, Bucks are relieved to be home for eight of the last 13 games. Then they start sweating Redd's free agency.
Word is that Porter is next in line on the Endangered Coaches List. The local paper, in fact, offers a poll asking fans if the coach should be brought back for a third season.
A long season has the potential to get longer. On April 18, Bucks must face Iverson one last time ... after surrendering at least 40 points to AI each of the first three times.
Does anyone remember that Bucks' season started 3-1? It certainly didn't help that Milwaukee, amid increasing sale and Redd's Leaving speculation, went 0-15 on the road vs. the West.

tor.summary: Mo Pete is now the league's reigning Iron Man at 260 consecutive games. Of course, in line with Raps' recent fortunes, you'll note that A.C. Green's record is 1,192 consecutive games.
Raps are 21-24 since trading Vince. Not bad, actually, but not good enough to close all wounds opened by Vince's renaissance.
Attn. folks who don't like our occasional bon mots for Pape: Send suggestions. Toronto is one of our favorite cities, but not much Raps-wise is happening up there these days. Is there?
People, people, people. Most of your suggestions were Bosh-related, a lefty we love and praise as much as Pape. Pumping Bosh up is nothing new in this cyberspace.
Stuff is happening anew. Bosh is a bit more outspoken, Vince returns to town Friday ... and Pape just got his first NBA start.
If Pape's starting, we'll be watching. We'll also be watching Wednesday's finale to track Cleveland's fate and see two of our favorite lefties for the last time 'til fall: Bosh and Jalen.

gsw.summary: Warriors finished a brutal eight-game trip at 4-4. They prefer to focus on that as opposed to Montgomery needing until March to secure his 20th victory. Not a good thing in the pros.
Who saw this coming? With two wins over Sacramento sandwiched around a road upset of Phoenix, Montgomery is suddenly having a better March than Stanford.
Montgomery says Baron is getting too much credit. Huh? GS is 6-4 on the road with Baron ... and 5-21 without him.
Trivia time: Who has the best record in Cali since the All-Star break? Yup: Warriors are 13-7; Lakers are last at 7-16.
Warriors desperately want to believe this late-season run means something for next season ... and that the draft choice affected by all this recent winning wouldn't be that helpful anyway.
They've faded a little, sure, since that record-setting road win streak. But it's been a fun ride since Baron arrived, as Ws over Suns (twice), Kings  (twice), Rockets and Sonics would suggest.

por.summary: In our ongoing quest to find anything nice to say here, try this: Stoudamire recently became just the second player shorter than 6-0 (after Calvin Murphy) to score 10,000 career points.
Pritchard says he wants to return to personnel work at season's end. Can't blame him: Blazers are 9-27 since a 14-14 start.
Talk about a drought. Blazers don't have a road win over a West foe since (ouch) Opening Night at Golden State.
Some Blazers news, at last, that we're excited to hear: Van Exel, one of our faves, has decided against retiring at season's end.
D. Stoudamire says Blazers losing more than 45 games for the first time since '73-74 feels ''worse'' than embarrassing. Since this isn't an expansion team like his 21-61 rookie-year Raps.
The kiddies' 2-14 mark in March -- the worst month in club history -- has given way to a 2-8 April. At least Portland should get a high draft pick for its season of suffering.

uta.summary: Fresh off what might be his best job ever -- 42-40 in his first season without Mailman and Stock -- Sloan is officially a losing coach for the first time since taking over Jazz in 1988.
The depths of Utah's struggles are simply hard to believe. Jerry Sloan has been stuck on 937 victories, one shy of tying Red Auerbach, since the first Jazz game of the month on March 2.
Raja Bell reluctantly conceded that Jazz have 'cashed it in.' Which tells you all you need to know about L.A.'s playoff chances when Lakers go to Utah and give up 115 points.
In this What Next season, now it's Boozer out for the season. Kirilenko was first, meaning that Utah's projected frontcourt stalwarts played just 25 games together in Year 1.
Utah's season peaked Nov. 13. Jazz and Sonics were tied atop the Northwest Division at 5-1 that day. But Seattle then won 14 of 18, Utah lost 15 of its next 21 and, well, now look.
Injuries were obviously a killer, but last season's  42-40 magic disappeared just before Thanksgiving ... when Jazz lost back-to-back home games to then-winless Hornets and Bulls.

nop.summary: It isn't much, but it's something: Hornets are 3-2 in March, which could easily be 4-1. Which means they might actually be pulling away from Charlotte and Atlanta.
Only four more chances remain to spruce up that 0-12 record against Southwest Division neighbors. One game each against Dallas and Memphis, and two more against Houston.
They did it! They did it! With only two chances remaining to finally beat a divisional foe, Hornets stun Memphis to improve to 1-13 against their fellow Southwest tenants.
How unikely was that win in Houston? Yao was out, true, but Hornets became the first team since Sonics in '76 to get 20 points or less from their starters (15 in this case) and still win.
Shinn can certainly answer critics by pointing out that this was Hornets' first losing season since '91-92. But they need to win at least one more game to avoid the worst season in club history.
It's all good. Owner George Shinn, in a recent letter to season-ticket holders, announced that ''I am committed to building a team that will be successful in New Orleans.'' No worries.

atl.summary: What a week. Hawks finally won a road game after 23 consecutive away defeats ... and Ty Lue topped the 25-point plateau in consecutive games for the first time in his career.
Well, it's back to reality after the breakthrough road triumph in Toronto. Hawks just completed an 0-4 homestand, surrendering no fewer than 106 points in any of the losses.
Hawks are on the verge of joining Clips of '86-87 (12-70) and 1947-48's Providence Steamrollers (6-42) as the only teams in history to go a whole season without winning two in a row.
Obinna Ekezie is Woodson's center and Royal Ivey is his point guard. Which is another way of saying that, yes, the rookie coach deserves the No. 1 overall pick for his suffering.
Driving the stake into Minnesota's season is only half of what Atlanta accomplished Saturday night. The big news is Hawks have finally surpassed Falcons' regular-season win total of 11.
At least they avoided 70 losses. Not by much, but Hawks -- after losing back-to-back games to Charlotte to make sure they have the most lottery pingpong balls -- achieved that much.

cha.summary: Since that crucial 10th victory, Bobcats are 2-16. The wins were good (Nuggets, Kings) but you have to wonder how low they can go after that fall-from-ahead, Kobe-inflicted heartbreak.
Yes, you guessed right: After a long lean spell, Bobcats have already circled their two Atlanta games next month.
Our math has never been as good as our father's -- you're the man, Reuvs -- but something tells us that the committee's 13-69 prediction for the expansionites is in trouble.
We're pulling for a surging Brevin Knight to get that assist average into double digits. The NBA hasn't had two 10-assist men since Stock and our man Mark Jackson in '96-97.
Oh, well. Even after averaging 11 apg over his past 11 games, Brevin Knight would need to average 19.5 dimes in Charlotte's final six games to get his average into double digits.
In the end, Bobs couldn't secure the first three-game win streak in club history. But seeing Bobs with 17 wins still shocks us almost as much as seeing Utah with only 25.
